:::{#def-bit}
#### Bit

A **bit** is the unit of information
when the logarithm in [surprisal](#def-surprisal),
and in every quantity built from it, has base $2$.

One bit is the surprisal of an outcome with probability $1/2$:
for an outcome $x$ of a discrete random variable $X$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
s(x) = 1 \text{ bit}
&\iff -\log_2 \P(X=x) = 1\\
&\iff \P(X=x) = 2^{-1} = \tfrac{1}{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

So one bit is the information in learning the value of
a random variable with two equally likely values,
such as one toss of a fair coin.

:::
